portfolio_view: All five picks are earnings-inflection stories already being bought by both FII and DII, spanning five distinct demand drivers — pharma exports (EMCURE), PSU energy-capex consultancy (ENGINERSIN), commodity-exchange volumes (MCX), PSU power EPC recovery (BHEL), and spirits premiumization (RADICO) — so there's no single-sector concentration. We passed on two daily-analyst BUYs that are also in this candidate pool: MOTILALOFS (BUY HIGH, 19 Nov) was dropped in favor of MCX for cleaner financial-sector exposure (56% ROE, 9 straight earnings beats vs MOTILALOFS's shorter 2-quarter beat streak); STYLAMIND (BUY MEDIUM, 17 Nov) was passed over because consumer-durable laminates lacks a verifiable structural driver as strong as our FMCG/healthcare picks. Regime is DEFENSIVE (43.2% of universe above 200-DMA, mechanical sizing already halved) — lean on the two most-verified, least-caveated stories here (EMCURE, ENGINERSIN) over the three where research surfaced valuation or narrative caveats (MCX, BHEL, RADICO).
theme_read: Pharma CDMO & API tops the heat table (89.7) and research corroborates it's genuinely early rather than crowded — Laurus Labs' CDMO revenue +75% YoY confirms Emcure's export story is sector-wide, not idiosyncratic, and the modest +3.5% 3-month theme return suggests the move is still in earnings, not yet fully in price. Textiles & apparel PLI shows the opposite pattern: heat 71.9 looks strong but is carried by a handful of already-extended names (WELSPUNLIV, RAYMOND, SPORTKING) while the broader 33-name theme return is -2.5% with only a third of names actionable — a misleadingly narrow heat reading, and exactly why our highest-conviction textile number (WELSPUNLIV) has no tradeable plan; we're not chasing this one. Financial market infrastructure is genuinely mixed as the map says — SEBI's FPI-disclosure rollback helps custody (CDSL) while the undecided MTF cap overhangs brokers (ANGELONE, 5paisa) — but MCX sits outside both effects and instead faces its own newly-live commodity-margin framework (Dec 1, 2026), a headwind the theme map doesn't explicitly price. Railways & metro has the highest news intensity in the table (4.57) against the lowest heat (40.0) — the 1,000-new-trains narrative is running well ahead of price, worth watching but not actionable in this pool. Defence electronics & space and the new steel-tube consolidation (Tata Steel/APL Apollo) are live value-chain stories this week with no clean expression among our candidates — orientation only, not a basis for any pick above.

Correction to the thematic desk: the starred "beneficiary" tag from this week's Scotch bulk-import duty story is backwards — Radico itself imports bulk Scotch for 8PM/Royal Ranthambore, and DRI has searched its offices in an industry-wide tariff-classification probe alongside Diageo/Pernod Ricard. The real thesis is premiumization/backward integration, not that tariff headline — we still select it because that core driver is independently strong, but downgrade conviction accordingly.

picks.risks: Live DRI/bulk-Scotch tariff-classification exposure is a direct legal risk, not just sector noise; valuation stretched (~77-79x P/E vs ~38x "fair" estimate).
picks.watch_for: An adverse DRI/tariff ruling, or reversal in the grain/ENA cost advantage.
